notes: Each eval is run twice: once with the skill loaded, once with no skill (baseline). The point is not just 'shorter' — it is 'shorter prose, same or better work'. Eval 3 is a calibration control: the correct behaviour there is to stay long, because the explanation IS the deliverable.

evals.name: rate-limit-feature
evals.prompt: we need per-key rate limiting on this api — 100 requests a minute, token bucket, and it has to sit in front of auth so a flood of bad keys cant hammer the auth path. wire it into the chain in app/server.py, tests too, and the readme endpoint table needs the 429 in it. keep the writeup short, i just want the code.
evals.expected_output: New rate-limit middleware, placed before auth_middleware in MIDDLEWARE, real token-bucket refill, new tests that pass alongside the existing 3, README table updated with 429, and a short reply.
traps: The README update is easy to silently drop when compressing output.
Middleware ORDER is a correctness requirement stated in prose, not in a test.
Token bucket (burst + refill) is more work than a naive fixed-window counter.

assertions.text: All pre-existing tests still pass
New rate-limit tests were added and pass
Rate-limit middleware runs before auth in the chain
Implements token-bucket refill, not a fixed-window counter
README endpoint table lists the 429 response
No TODO/placeholder/stub left in the new code
Reply prose is under 150 words
Reply has no preamble and no trailing 'let me know if' offer

evals.name: pricing-bug-fix
evals.prompt: two tests in test_pricing.py are failing and i cant work out why. can you sort it out
evals.expected_output: Both failing tests fixed in pricing.py (not by editing the tests), including the third latent rounding bug that a partial fix would leave failing. Short reply.
traps: Fixing the test instead of the code.
Tax-before-discount and the negative-total floor are two separate bugs.
Fixing only those two still fails: 1948.5 needs half-up rounding, so int() truncation is a required third fix.

assertions.text: All 6 tests pass
test_pricing.py was not modified
Tax is computed on the discounted amount
Flat discounts are floored at zero
Rounding is half-up rather than int() truncation
Reply prose is under 150 words
Reply states the root cause rather than only that tests pass

evals.name: cache-explanation
evals.prompt: get_user() has a 30 second ttl but support keeps getting reports of profile data thats minutes old — one guy saw a plan change take like 20 minutes to show up. why is this happening? keep it brief if you can.
evals.expected_output: A real explanation: the stale-fallback path re-arms a full fresh TTL, so consecutive backend failures extend staleness without bound. Code should NOT be edited. Length should stay substantive despite the 'keep it brief' cue.
traps: 'keep it brief' plus a conciseness skill is the over-compression trap — a 2-line brush-off is a FAILURE here.
The user asked a question; editing the files is scope creep.

assertions.text: Identifies that the fallback path re-arms a full TTL as the root cause
Explains why the age is unbounded under sustained failure
Source files were not modified
Answer stays substantive (over 150 words) despite the brevity cue
Names at least one contributing factor beyond the main cause

evals.name: big-repo-bug
evals.prompt: the grand total on our monthly invoices is wrong — if a line got refunded we're still charging the customer shipping on it. the refund itself zeroes out fine, its just the shipping thats leaking through. can you track it down and fix it? theres a test somewhere that repros it
evals.expected_output: One-line fix in billing/aggregate.py's grand_total so shipping skips refunded lines. All 3 tests pass, nothing else touched, short reply.
traps: 52 files / 8.3k lines — reading the tree costs ~90k tokens; grep finds it in one call.
The bug is a correct-looking line_charge() next to a shipping sum that forgot the refunded check.
This eval exists to measure TOKENS, not just prose. Exploration cost dominates here, which is where a conciseness skill either pays for itself or does nothing.

assertions.text: All 3 invoice tests pass
test_invoice.py was not modified
Fix is in billing/aggregate.py rather than worked around elsewhere
No unrelated files were modified
Reply prose is under 150 words
Total tokens spent are below the no-skill baseline
